findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method added in this PR is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and no no-arg overload exists in this class or in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. This does not compile, so the whole services module fails to build. Either add a no-arg overload (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) or pass `context.getUser()` here.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, inverting the previous behaviour and disabling conditional passkeys on the first login screen
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was executed exactly when `context.getUser() == null` (authenticate(), old else-branch) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` when the user was not yet selected. With the new helper, both call sites (lines 115 and 137) now do the opposite: the WebAuthn/conditional-UI data is only filled when a user is already set (re-authentication), and is never filled for a plain login where no user has been established yet. Consequently the normal passkeys autofill/conditional-UI on the initial username+password page disappears (no challenge, no rpId, no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI), which breaks the primary passkeys login flow and the existing assertions in these tests that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page. The condition most likely should be `user == null || user has a passwordless WebAuthn credential` rather than `user != null`.

findings.title: Unconditionally returning false removes the guard that skipped the passkey form for users without WebAuthn credentials
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` is overridden to always return false. In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` this branch also contained the check `if (authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()) return null;`, which prevented rendering passkey UI for an identified user that has no WebAuthn credential. Since the conditional-UI authenticator is now also used while a user is already set (re-authentication), a user who only has a password but belongs to a realm with passkeys enabled will now get the passkey/conditional-UI markup rendered on the re-authentication form (with IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false and no allowCredentials), so any passkey attempt can only fail or, worse, let the browser offer a discoverable credential of a different user which then aborts the flow with WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER. The 'no credentials' case should still suppress the passkey UI.

findings.title: No test for re-authentication of a passkey-less user while passkeys are enabled for the realm
findings.body: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` only sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`, i.e. it verifies the trivial case where passkeys are disabled realm-wide. The behaviour actually changed by this PR is re-authentication with passkeys *enabled* for the realm: in that case `fillContextForm` is now invoked for an already-identified user, and because `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` returns false the previous 'user has no WebAuthn credential' short-circuit no longer applies. There is no test covering a user that has only a password while realm passkeys are enabled, which is exactly the regression-prone path.

findings.title: Broad catch(Exception) around element lookup can make the assertion vacuous
findings.body: The two `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { }` blocks (lines 291-296 and 312-317) swallow any RuntimeException from WebDriver, not just NoSuchElementException (e.g. StaleElementReferenceException or a WebDriver timeout), so the test can pass without ever proving the webauthn form is absent. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` as done in the other tests in this package.
